column1: # Chat spellings of common Hindi words that the tables don't reach: latin<TAB>hindi.
# Hand-written for this repository from how people write Hindi in Latin letters, not taken
# from any dataset; see data/manifests/chat-forms-hi.json. The Hindi pack's "chatForms" file,
# read by the engine (engine/core/src/chat_forms.rs). A typed word matching a row (ignoring
# case) offers its Hindi word as if the letters spelled it out; a swipe through a row's
# Only spellings that belong to one word go here. A habit that holds across words is for
# romanisation.json: the final anusvara and chandrabindu left unwritten (nahi, hu, me, logo)
# are its optionalFinals, so no row here is needed for them.
# क्यों (why) walks as kyon; it is said with a short, nasal o and written kyu or kyun far
# more often than kyon or kyo. The same in क्योंकि (because).
# यह (this) and वह (that) are spelled as they are said, yeh and woh; the walk gives yah and
# vah. Without a row yeh reaches only ये, and woh no Hindi word at all.
# हम (we) and its forms: the short a is written u, as in English "hum". The walk gives ham.
# Typed, any u between consonants may stand for that vowel (romanisation.json's
# alsoBetweenConsonants), behind words with a real u; a swipe can't afford that for every
# word, so the forms of this one, which are among the most written, are listed.
# बहुत (very): the a before h is said and written o. The walk gives bahut.
